messages:
sara-cs: Customer sent a short screen recording and says the app 'hangs then fails' with no error message. They are non-technical. What's the simplest one-line ask we can give so they can grab a request/trace ID?

luis-eng: Short ask that non-devs can do: 'Open Network, refresh, find the failed request, and copy the response header called X-Request-Id (or Copy as cURL)'. I'll write a tiny script for them if needed.

maria-support: I'll paste a step-by-step they can follow in a friendly way. Keep it 3 bullets max and give UI screenshots pointers.

sara-cs: Yes please — also ask for the approximate local time of the replay and the email used so we can match logs. :pray:

maria-support: Customer-facing text (keep exact):
- Please open the app/browser and reproduce the problem.
- If you're on a browser: press F12 (or open DevTools) > Network tab > Refresh the page.
- In the list, look for a request to "api.redwood" or any request that failed (status 4xx/5xx). Click it, then in the Response Headers find "X-Request-Id" or "x-request-id" and paste that value here.
If you can't find it, right-click the failing request and choose "Copy" → "Copy as cURL" and paste the whole cURL.

customer-jane: I tried but couldn't find headers. I copied the cURL instead, here it is (redacted):
```
curl 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-raw '{"input":"hello"}'
```

luis-eng: Perfect — that cURL is enough. From our side we can extract the timestamp and route. Can you also include the exact local time you made that request (approx to the minute) and the email/user id?

maria-support: If they're on mobile (app): tell them to record a 10–15s screen video showing the step where they trigger the request, and then send it. For iOS/android guide: Settings → Help → Send Feedback often includes a network capture option in our SDKs; if not, the screen video plus approximate time works.

sara-cs: Also ask them to run one tiny confirmatory step: open the app, reproduce once, then paste the value of the error message they see (even if it's just 'Something went wrong'). Small details help.

luis-eng: On our side we'll search for that X-Request-Id or for requests around the provided timestamp and route. If we need more we may ask them to:
- Open DevTools > Network > right-click request > Save all as HAR and attach the HAR file.
- Or paste the cURL. HAR preferred but cURL is fine.

maria-support: Short troubleshooting checklist I'll send the customer (copy this):
1) Reproduce and paste X-Request-Id (or copy-as-cURL).
2) Tell us local time of the attempt, email/account, and model/feature used (e.g., chat, embeddings).
3) If possible attach a 10s screen recording showing the attempt.
4) If you can save a HAR file from the browser that's the fastest to triage.

sara-cs: Sending now. Thanks — tagging @luis-eng in case you want to pre-search logs once the customer replies.

redwood-bot: Reminder: please redact API keys when pasting cURL or HAR files. Bots will flag any detected secrets.

customer-jane: Ok — found the header in DevTools: X-Request-Id = 8f2b9a7c. I also attached a 12s video and my approximate time was 2024-11-03 14:22 UTC. Email: jane+acme@example.com. Hope this helps!

luis-eng: Got it — thanks @customer-jane and @sara-cs. We'll correlate 8f2b9a7c + 2024-11-03 14:22 UTC and report back with a minimal repro and root cause within the hour.

maria-support: Closing loop once eng confirms. :white_check_mark:
